text:
support-jen: Heads-up — customer on Next.js SSR hitting runtime `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` and our SDK failing to load in production. They see a flurry of 5xxs and repeated retries from the app. Repro steps attached below.

devex-tyler: Thanks Jen. Is this the hosted API or dedicated? Any errors from our side (401/429)?

support-jen: Hosted API. No 401/429 on our logs — just their server throwing `Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: Must use import to load ES Module` when doing SSR. They say local dev (next dev) works fine, issue only after `next build && next start`.

alex: Can you paste their package.json exports + the SDK version they installed? Also node version for prod.

support-jen: Sure. From customer: 
```json
{
  "name": "web-app",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood-inference/sdk": "^1.4.0"
  },
  "engines": {"node": ">=18.0.0"}
}
```
And their `@redwood-inference/sdk` package.json snippet: 
```json
"main": "dist/index.cjs",
"module": "dist/index.mjs",
"types": "dist/index.d.ts",
"exports": {
  "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
  "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
}
```
They also bundle with `next` (webpack) during `next build` — server runtime Node 18 on host.

maria: This smells like conditional exports + bundler resolution mismatch. Webpack (used by Next) sometimes resolves the `import` entry when building for SSR if config targets modern syntax, which can cause runtime to attempt to load ESM in a CJS runtime or vice versa. The `types` pointing to `dist/index.d.ts` is fine but if bundler inlines code path, server can still expect CJS.

devex-tyler: Do they get `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` when Node tries to require the `.mjs` file? Any stack trace?

support-jen: Short stack: `at Object.<anonymous> (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1078:13)`, then `at Module._compile`. They also show Next server log where the import is attempted via `require('./node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/index.mjs')`.

alex: Repro locally: `npm i next @redwood-inference/sdk@1.4.0 && npx next build && NODE_ENV=production npx next start` — do we see same error? We should try to reproduce with Node 18 and webpack target `es2020`.

maria: Quick mitigation: ask customer to set an explicit conditional export for node resolution. Example recommended change in our SDK package.json: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "node": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" },
    "default": "./dist/index.cjs"
  }
}
```
This helps bundlers pick the right entry for Node SSR. Also adding a `main` fallback is useful.

support-jen: Customer tried pinning to 1.3.2 and error went away. 1.4.0 introduced an exports-only layout. They don't want to pin long-term.

devex-tyler: Okay, sounds like 1.4.0 changed exports shape and lost a `main` fallback that webpack/next were relying on. Need an eng runtime patch. @alex / @maria can you confirm if we should release a 1.4.1 with a node-targeted conditional export and `main` fallback?

alex: I'll prepare a patch. For support playbook, ask customers to: 1) pin SDK to the last known-good minor, 2) ensure Node 18+ and no custom transpiler that forces `import` resolution, 3) as temporary workaround add `webpack: { experiments: { topLevelAwait: false }}` — but note that's a hack.

maria: Also log a follow-up: add CI test that installs our SDK into a minimal Next.js app and runs `next build` to detect packaging regressions.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: patches/sdk-1.4.1 (rollback-fix-exports) — CI 24/50 passed (running integration nextjs packaging test).

support-jen: I'll tell the customer to pin and that we're shipping 1.4.1. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
